segments.english: Reply. I ask of my God that He lead me in paths of straightness and rescue us from a lying lip, from a deceitful tongue. Teach me, LORD, Your ways; I will walk in Your truth. Unite my heart to fear Your name. And send Your light and Your truth; they will lead me to answer a word spoken in its settings. Roll reproach and scorn away from me, for I have kept Your testimonies. Even though princes sit and speak against me, Your servant meditates on Your statutes. Then I shall not be ashamed, when I do not turn aside from the way that our Rabbis of blessed memory taught us, the masters of the Mishnah and the Talmud and the true midrashim and the decisors who follow in their footsteps, on whom all the house of Israel lean. For they are the masters of the true tradition, who received from Moses our teacher the generalities and particulars of the Torah, upon which he stood at Sinai forty days and forty nights, and handed them to Joshua, and Joshua to the elders, etc., as is stated in tractate Avot. 1) And it is a holy duty incumbent on us to follow in their footsteps in everything that yields a practical difference in law: in all matters of forbidden and permitted, impure and pure, unfit and fit. All the more so in matters of the unity of the Name, may He be blessed, which is the great principle, and after it the tradition of all the commandments and how they are to be done, as the Tanna, peace be upon him, said: "Why did the section of Shema precede 'And it shall be, if you hearken, etc.!'" And any author of a book who comes to add to or subtract from their words, and all the more so to turn us from the faith of the holy Torah according to the tradition of our rabbis, the masters of the Mishnah and the Talmud, we will not hearken to him. And even if he performs signs and wonders in heaven and on earth, we will not turn aside from following the LORD our God, according to the tradition of our Rabbis of blessed memory, the masters of the Mishnah and the Talmud and the decisors who come after them and follow in their footsteps. And even if from heaven a bat kol calls, hearken to him, to depart from their tradition, we shall not heed it, as Rabbi Yehoshua said: "One does not heed a bat kol, for it is not in heaven."

tokens.note: תשובה (2:34.1) is the label of the reply; the prayer begins with אשאלה, 'I will ask', whose object is the clause ינחני 'that He lead me'
the Tetragrammaton as written (ה׳ in Ps 86:11), read in context as the LORD
printed אפניו; Prov 25:11 has אופניו (see apparatus)
רז"ל = רבותינו זכרונם לברכה
הקבלה: the word the Kabbalists use for their own lore; the author claims it here for the Mishnah and Talmud
ממרע"ה = משה רבנו עליו השלום
printed list marker א) (aleph = 1), kept as the author's own: 1)
Aramaic idiom מידי דנפקא מינה לדינא, 'anything with a practical difference in law'

וכ"ש = וכל שכן, 'all the more so'. The Hebrew sentence has no main clause after a full stop (the Hebrew leaves one implicit); proposed ruling: keep the fragment as the author's syntax and add no verb, or join it to the previous sentence with a semicolon ('...unfit and fit; and all the more so in matters of the unity of the Name...'). The owner to decide.

grammar: תשובה: the label of the reply, as at 2:3, 2:7 and 2:28 of the correspondence; אשאלה מאלהי ינחני: 'I will ask of my God that He lead me'; the paragraph is a prayer in the author's own voice, addressed to the LORD.
The Psalm verses are run into the author's sentences without a formula: הוריני (Ps 86:11), ושלח (Ps 43:3), גל (Ps 119:22) and גם כי ישבו (Ps 119:23), so they take no quotation marks.
אז לא אבוש כאשר לא אסור מן הדרך: the main clause is 'then I shall not be ashamed'; כאשר is a temporal clause, 'when I do not turn aside'.

אשר למדונו רז"ל ... בעלי המשנה ... ההולכים בעקבותיהם is a relative clause on הדרך: the way that the Sages taught us, with the authorities in apposition; אשר כל בית ישראל נשענים עליהם is a second relative clause on the same authorities.

The Tanna's question, 'למה קדמה פרשת שמע לוהיה אם שמוע וכו'!', is quoted in the author's words and truncated with וכו'; the author then argues a fortiori (וכ"ש) from matters of law to the unity of the Name, and from the unity to the rejection of an author who alters the tradition.

Aramaic idioms in the author's Hebrew: מידי דנפקא מינה לדינא ('what yields a practical difference in law') and לא משגחינן בה ('we do not heed it'); the Tanna's question about the Shema is Mishnaic Hebrew, and R. Yehoshua's saying is the Talmud's.
segments.note: The author's prayer opens the paragraph, then his claim for the tradition of the Mishnah, Talmud and decisors. The English keeps 'us' where the Hebrew has ויצילנו; the Psalm allusions are in apparatus.
apparatus: Base text from Wikisource; the 1931 scan is not yet collated (Wikisource additions, Q2).
Ps 120:2 (embedded): משפת שקר, מלשון רמיה. The psalm has 'my soul' where the author writes ויצילנו (us).
Ps 23:3 (embedded allusion): ינחני במעגלי צדק; the author writes יושר.
Ps 86:11 (embedded): הוריני ה' דרכיך אהלך באמתך; יחד לבבי ליראה שמך.
Ps 43:3 (embedded): ושלח אורך ואמתך המה ינחוני.
Prov 25:11 (embedded): דבר דבור על אופניו. The author prints אפניו; the verse has אופניו.
Ps 119:22: גל מעלי חרפה ובוז כי עדותיך נצרתי.
Ps 119:23: גם כי ישבו שרים בי נדברו, עבדך ישיח בחוקיך.
Deut 11:13: והיה אם שמוע תשמעו, the opening of the second paragraph of the Shema; the author writes לוהיה.
Deut 13:2-5 (embedded allusion): אות ומופת; לא תשמע אל דברי הנביא ההוא; אחרי ה' אלהיכם תלכו.
Deut 10:10 (embedded allusion; cf. Deut 9:9): עמדתי בהר ... ארבעים יום וארבעים לילה.
Deut 30:12: לא בשמים היא, the verse on which Rabbi Yehoshua's saying rests.
2:34.199 לבור (printed): probably לעבור, 'to pass from', with the ע dropped (cf. 'to depart from their tradition'); translated by the sense of the context. The Hebrew לבור does not mean 'depart'.
context: Bat kol (literally 'daughter of a voice') is the rabbinic term for a voice from heaven. The saying the author cites, by Rabbi Yehoshua, holds that such a voice is not heeded in matters of law, since it is not in heaven.
